references.text: Here is told the story of Zelophehad's daughters who claimed inheritance rights, which led to the law that daughters could inherit when there were no sons. This is the basis for why Manasseh's daughters inherited land.

Elaborates on the rules for inheritance through daughters and the requirement that they must marry within their own tribe to preserve the inheritance, directly linked to Zelophehad's daughters from the tribe of Manasseh.
Specifically mentions Zelophehad's daughters and their inheritance among the sons of Manasseh, which is the immediate context for verse 6.
Describes how Gilead was given to Machir, son of Manasseh, as background for why Gilead belonged to the remaining sons of Manasseh.
Moses describes the distribution of Gilead and Bashan to the half-tribe of Manasseh, confirming their ownership of the Gilead region.
Earlier description of the territory given to the half-tribe of Manasseh, including Gilead.
The genealogy of Manasseh that mentions Zelophehad's daughters and their inheritance confirms that they inherited among the men of the tribe.
